messages.author: 66c619563770f0f5
messages.subject: AMOVA
parts:
My script to run AMOVA after converting a Structure file is as follows:

amova<-read.structure ("~/Desktop/HARENDRA/structure1.str")
strata(amova) <- data.frame(Pop = pop(amova)) # create the strata of ppopualation.MUST
head(strata(amova))        # show the results
amova1<- as.genclone(amova)
amova1
table(strata(amova1, ~Pop))  # to look at the different stratifications, populations or subpopulations
## Actual AMOVA
AMOVAamova<-poppr.amova(amova, ~Pop, missing = "ignore")

Do I need to use distance to define?

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] AMOVA
parts:
Hi Rajendra,

No, you do not need to define a distance. Poppr will calculate the distance automatically as a euclidean transformation of the number of differences between individuals.


If you want to include a custom distance (i.e. Bruvo's distance), you can use the dist argument. See here for more details: https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/poppr/versions/2.3.0/topics/poppr.amova

Best,
Zhian
